note: Engine-level tests in the candidate harness (/tmp/cand). Gain = mean log-likelihood per race vs Engine v2.3 (res_C2_R) on the same races; A = 2024 validation (12,777 races), B = 2025-26 (23,729 races, re-used period). Point in time; no prices.

STD_state_standardised_margins.what: margins converted to seconds with each state's measured s/L (Qld 0.170, SA 0.1595, Vic 0.1619; NSW/WA/Tas/ACT left at the national figure, no assumption), then back to national lengths before the rating
STD_state_standardised_margins.verdict: slightly worse in both windows: do not introduce state margin corrections
STD_state_standardised_margins.rerun_check: re-run 27 Nov 11:46 as STD2 (explicitly on the v2.3 harness history): identical result; the harness sandbox always reads its own v2.3 history file, so the first run was like-for-like

C2S_plus_suit_kernel_distance_suitabilit.what: horse's own past surprises weighted by closeness of distance (Gaussian, 150 m), shrunk with 3 pseudo-runs, added as one third-layer term
C2S_plus_suit_kernel_distance_suitabilit.verdict: no gain: the engine's existing distance terms already carry it (the rating-level residual of +0.19 to +0.21 kg is absorbed)

C2X_plus_xstate_interstate_level_term.what: for a run whose previous run was in another state, the average rating error of earlier movers on that state pair (estimated only from runs before 2024, shrunk n/(n+200)); 0 otherwise
C2X_plus_xstate_interstate_level_term.verdict: no material gain: interstate rating offsets exist at the rating level (SA, Qld and Tas horses rated about 0.4-1.5 kg high against Vic/NSW) but the engine already prices them; do not add state corrections

interstate_rating_offsets_by_frame.reading: standardising margins does not change the interstate offsets (they are not a margin-unit effect); the update rule narrows them slightly

PW_precision_weighted_race_reference.what: a race's level set mainly by the runners whose ratings are most certain (weights 1 / (rating variance + run noise)), instead of every runner counted equally; otherwise Engine v2.3
PW_precision_weighted_race_reference.verdict: small gain, clear only in the re-used 2025-26 window; not a candidate on its own; tested on top of the update rule next

B8_class_change_input_bm_change.what: Engine v2.3 structure in the harness: (a) fitted with bm_change and judged with it present (as if served), (b) fitted with it, judged with it missing (as production serves it today), (c) retrained without it
B8_class_change_input_bm_change.verdict: serving it would make chances worse (confirms Batch 15); but removing it from training is ALSO worse than today (-0.0008 / -0.0005, both clear): fitted with it, it acts as a training-only control that keeps the other inputs from soaking up class moves. Keep as is; record it as a training-only control. Reverses the earlier plan to drop it at the next release

U5PW_precision_reference_on_top_of_updat.what: update rule (cap 12 L in the figure, good runs 1.3x) plus the certainty-weighted race level
U5PW_precision_reference_on_top_of_updat.verdict: small, clear in both windows, one pre-specified variant (no tuning): candidate to fold into the update rule at its next refit; the shadow is not changed now
